decisions.statement: A seat comes up under tmux.
A terminal that quits leaves the seat working.
The launch is composed from the same recipe the program launching a seat uses.
A session is live only where that session has a pane that is not dead.
A session with only a dead pane is stopped and started again.
A tmux server this socket does not reach stops the launch rather than stranding.
A resume attaches to a live session a page states, asking nothing to start it.
A live session no page states is resumed rather than attached to.
Whether a seat is stated is read as the page that seat's name reaches.
A fresh seat stops whatever held its name before that seat starts.
A name held by a tmux session with no seat page is stopped as that session.
A stop refused for anything but a missing page stops the launch.
One word naming a persona with no document is split into a name.
A word naming a person rather than a persona seats that person's handler.
A seat bound to no agent id is not launched.
A seat's attributes are stated before its client comes up.
Starting a seat is asked of the akasha command by name.

definition: the shell starting a fresh seat or resuming one, attached in the terminal typed in
